cohort: 160 pregnant patients who presented to an antenatal outpatient or emergency department with reduced fetal movements, excluding those in active labor.
finding: The study identified reduced liquor and abnormal umbilical artery Doppler as primary causes of reduced fetal movements, which were associated with increased neonatal unit admission rates, higher induction and cesarean section rates, and increased perinatal morbidity and mortality despite a higher number of live births.
mod_finding: The study found that reduced fetal movements resulted in higher induction and cesarean section rates.
followup_time: Until delivery and early neonatal period
birth_weight: Babies included had average (76.25%), low (20%), and very low (3.12%) birth weights.
gest_age: Pregnant patients presented between 30-40 weeks gestation, with the majority (83.12%) at 36-40 weeks.
